chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami and Zayd al-Shahham, and Mansur ibn Hazim, said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered us that we should exclaim the Talbiyya and not specify anything, and he said: 'The people of the concealment in the mind are more beloved to me.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الْإِضْمَارِ: the people of concealment in the mind (referring to keeping intention internal)
key_terms.أَنْ نُلَبِّيَ: that we should exclaim the Talbiyya

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred method for reciting the Talbiyya during Ihram prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural nuance of the Ihram prayer by instructing companions to recite the Talbiyya generally ('Labbayk') without specifying the type of pilgrimage, reflecting the Shia preference for simplicity and avoiding unnecessary restriction. Furthermore, it highlights the superiority of 'Ismar' (silent recitation/intention) over vocalization, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence that emphasizes the internal state of devotion over external performance.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy and Zayd Al Shahham, and Mansour Bin Hazim who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws ordered us that we should exclaim Talbiyya and not to specify anything. And heasws said: ‘The people of the concealment in the mind are more beloved to me (than the ones speaking their intentions)’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from abu Bakr al- Hadramiy and Zayd al-Shahham and from Mansur ibn Hazim who have said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, commanded us to say Talbiyah and do not mention any name. He (the Imam) said, ‘People who do not mention are more likeable to me.’”
